speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: Better connectivity for people, goods, information and capital allows us to attract new ideas, talent and investments and opens up new markets for Singapore firms.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: As we expand Singapore's connections to the rest of the world via our air and sea ports, it is equally important to strengthen our links closer to home.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: Current connectivity with our nearest neighbour, Malaysia, is good.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: The Kuala Lumpur (KL)-Singapore High Speed Rail (HSR) and the Johor-Singapore Rapid Transit System, or RTS Link, will take this connectivity to a new level.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: The Prime Ministers of the two countries have called these "game changers".

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: They will draw our peoples and countries closer together, with a greater stake in each other's continued growth and success.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: It can be more convenient than flying and will be much faster than driving.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: It will be possible to go to KL for a day trip or business meeting, have our meeting there, have lunch there even, and still get home in time, in good time for dinner.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: It will, therefore, ease traffic volume along the Causeway and the Second Link, freeing up capacity for more goods to flow.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: Implementation of the HSR is already well under way.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: Both countries signed the HSR Bilateral Agreement in 2016.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: Since then, officials from both countries have been working closely to develop detailed plans for the construction, operation and regulation of the HSR.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: We have received strong indications of interest from key players from different countries and we look forward to meeting this key project milestone.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: As for the RTS Link, we are completing our joint advanced engineering studies.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: We expect to move swiftly into implementation after the signing of the Bilateral Agreement at the end of this year.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: It will be an exciting few years ahead, as we work alongside our Malaysian counterparts to gear up not just for one, but for two cross-border railway projects.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: The Ministry of Transport (MOT) proposes to enact the new Cross-Border Railways (CBR) Bill to enable the construction, operation and regulation of our cross-border railway projects within Singapore borders.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: Malaysia will likewise consider how best to implement these terms in their domestic legislation.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: The first part of the Bill pertains to the planning and construction of cross-border railways within Singapore.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: Clauses 4 to 6 set out the process to develop and finalise plans and maps for the construction of cross-border railways.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: This ensures transparency and accountability in the planning of cross-border railways, even as we strive to meet our ambitious timelines for completion.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: Plans and maps clearly showing the railway area and any land affected by construction of cross-border railways must be approved by the Chief Planner and made available to the public for inspection, just as what we do today for the construction of domestic Mass Rapid Transit (MRT) lines.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: Detailed plans for both the HSR and the RTS Link are being developed and we expect to finalise them in accordance with these provisions in the coming year or so.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: In line with the approach for constructing MRT and Light Rail Transit (LRT) lines under the Rapid Transit Systems Act today, clauses 7 to 16 will enable the Land Transport Authority (LTA) to access land for the purposes of constructing, operating and maintaining cross-border railways.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: As per current practice, notice will be given to affected landowners of any works.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: Should landowners suffer any damages to their land or structures on the land, they will be eligible for compensation under the Fourth Schedule of the Land Transport Authority of Singapore Act, similar to other Acts under LTA's purview today.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: In September, LTA has incorporated a wholly-owned subsidiary, SG HSR Pte Ltd, to be Singapore's Infrastructure Company, or InfraCo, for the HSR project.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: This arrangement allows us to dedicate resources to the development of the HSR, while allowing LTA to maintain its focus on domestic priorities.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: Accordingly, clauses 18 to 20 allow the Minister for Transport to give effect to an arrangement where an entity other than LTA is appointed as Singapore's InfraCo to build, fund, own and maintain the cross-border railway infrastructure within Singapore.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: This allows SG HSR Pte Ltd to exercise the powers at clauses 7 to 14 in place of LTA, where necessary, to fulfil its responsibilities in the HSR project.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: Taken together, these provisions enable LTA to coordinate the planning and construction of cross-border railways expeditiously to meet the targeted completion of the RTS Link by end-2024, and the HSR by end-2026.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: The second part of the Bill sets out a framework to give effect to the regulatory approach for our cross-border railway projects, which will focus on safety and security of operations.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: Commercial arrangements, such as the performance standards for the HSR and RTS Link services, will not be stipulated in legislation.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: Instead, they will be specified separately in contractual agreements signed between the respective commercial entities.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: To facilitate such an approach, clauses 21 to 29 set out the contractual arrangements that define two key functions in cross-border railway operations.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: Specifically, clauses 25 and 29 require any entity performing either of these functions to obtain a licence before it can provide services for passenger train operations.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: First, the entity providing and maintaining railway assets for operation of cross-border passenger train services is referred to in the Bill as the "Railway Assets Operator".

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: Second, the entity operating cross-border passenger train services is referred to as the "Train Service Operator".

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: LTA will regulate these functions for each cross-border railway entity through the general licensing provisions set out at clauses 30 to 44.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: This includes provisions that empower LTA to issue codes of practice, directions and provisional orders to ensure safe and secure cross-border railway operations.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: To ensure the safety and security of cross-border railway operations, this Bill includes provisions to empower authorised officers to inspect, investigate and enforce regulatory requirements.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: Clauses 49 to 53 set out the investigation and enforcement powers available to officers appointed by LTA as rail safety inspectors and independent safety auditors.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: Clause 58 empowers the Minister for Transport to appoint a cross-border railway security agency to coordinate security matters for cross-border railways.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: The cross-border railway security agency will work closely with the Ministry of Home Affairs and Home Team departments to issue and enforce security requirements for cross-border railways.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: This includes passenger checks required at the station, and standard procedures for responding to security incidents.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: This will facilitate coordination of security measures and requirements across domestic public transport and cross-border railway operations.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: To implement the regulatory framework proposed in this Bill, we will also be making related amendments to other Acts.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: In particular, the Land Transport Authority of Singapore Act will be amended to broaden LTA's functions to cover cross-border railway construction, operation and regulation.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: The compensation framework in the LTA Act will also be broadened to cover compensation that affected landowners may be eligible for under this Bill.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: The Railways Act and Rapid Transit Systems Act will be amended to clarify their scope.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: In particular, the Rapid Transit Systems Act applies only to domestic MRTs and LRTs.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: The Railways Act does not apply to any MRT or LRT that comes under the Rapid Transit Systems Act nor the HSR and RTS Link, which will come under the CBR Bill.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: As a whole, the regulatory framework in the new Bill largely takes reference from our domestic railway experience but is adapted to suit the unique commercial and regulatory requirements of the HSR and RTS Link Projects.

speaker: The Second Minister for Transport (Mr Ng Chee Meng)
text: There will be new business opportunities, greater access to resources and more travel options to the Malaysian hinterland.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Both the HSR and RTS will likely enhance cross-border trade and labour movement.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I will first touch on equity control provisions.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: There is a very detailed section on what it means to be an associate or subsidiary for purposes of determining direct or indirect controller of an entity.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Any person intending to dispose interest that would result in that person's shareholding falling below 75% or 50% of the total interest in a designated entity will be required to obtain prior approval from MPA.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: When I asked for the rationale for the introduction of such onerous requirements, Senior Minister of State Dr Lam Pin Min said the following – and please do bear with me as I quote from him below as I think the rationale he has explained provided justification for the Government to introduce these controls – and I quote: "The intention of the equity control requirements is not to interfere with the day-to-day operations of the designated entities or restrict its commercial flexibility, but rather to require MPA's approval to be sought for transactions crossing stipulated significant thresholds in equity interest.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Under the Companies Act, a 5% shareholder is considered a substantial shareholder.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Although a 5% shareholder typically does not have significant powers to drastically influence the direction of a company, it is still important for MPA to be informed of any new substantial shareholders of its designated public licensees.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Shareholders with 25% or 50% interest, however, wield significant voting power in a company's decisions.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: A shareholder who has more than 25% equity interest can veto special resolutions under the Companies Act.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: A shareholder with more than 50% equity interest can pass ordinary resolutions.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: These are the reasons why MPA should have some regulatory oversight on shareholders seeking to reach 25% and 50% of the equity interest respectively.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: On the other hand, a shareholder will lose its ability to control special resolutions if its equity interest falls below 75%.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: It will lose its ability to control ordinary resolutions if its equity interest falls below 50%.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: As these are important corporate decisions that could impact the overall direction of the company, MPA should maintain oversight on whether it is in our national interest for any incumbent shareholders to relinquish such voting powers… The acquisition controls enable MPA to have oversight of single persons becoming a new major shareholder of a designated entity.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The disposal controls grant MPA oversight of existing shareholders from selling interest in a designated entity, whether to a single or multiple persons." Mr Speaker, Sir, having heard the Senior Minister of State on his justifications for the equity controls provisions in the MPA Bill, I wonder whether there are any reasons why the same equity controls provisions are deemed not necessary for the CBR Bill.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The CBR Bill is an important Bill providing for the construction, maintenance, operation and regulation of cross-border railways between Singapore and Malaysia.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The Bill provides that the Government may enter into a concession agreement relating to the construction, maintenance, operation and improvement of the railway infrastructure of a cross-border railway with what is called a concessionaire.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: The Bill further provides for the concessionaire to appoint and enter into contract with one railway assets operator and a train service operator, both of whom are supposed to be regulated under the proposed Bill.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: If one regards container or port terminal operators to be important enough to be subject to approvals for equity changes under the MPA Act, then surely, for a Bill like the present one involving, say, one operator to be the railway assets operator and another one operator to be the train service operator, there is definitely a cause for the Government to impose similar equity control requirements.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: There will be concerns relating to customs, immigration and, of course, security as we are talking of many trains travelling between two countries on a daily basis.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: There may also be issues of economic security as we would like the train system to run profitably and efficiently.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: As this is a cross-border railway and in this climate where terrorist threats cannot be ruled out, the operators will need to pay attention and take steps to ensure the security of the rail assets and infrastructure as well as the security of the services and the passengers, staff as well as other users of the rail assets and facilities.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: We need to be assured of the shareholding of the companies who are concessionaires, licensees or operators, lest they fall into wrong hands and bring unnecessary risks and consequences.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I look forward to the Minister’s reply on this.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Next, I will touch on the acquisition of private land.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Clause 8 of the Bill empowers LTA to, for purposes of constructing the railways or building-related infrastructure, enter private land and take possession of the land, and carry out acts like removing any building or structure, digging tunnel and constructing railway facilities.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: These are serious interferences with the rights of an owner of a private property.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: If the work that is going to be done under this clause compels the owners to have to stop living there or to stop their businesses on the land, the Government should give a longer notice.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: When a person decides to buy a private property, it will normally take up to about 10 weeks to 12 weeks for the conveyancing process, that is, the legal process for the transfer of title, to complete.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: So, if a two-month notice is given under this clause, the owner of the property will probably not be able to have sufficient time to buy another property and complete the conveyancing process, not to mention to have time to look around for a suitable replacement property or time to do renovations for the new property.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Is the Minister able to provide any indication at this point that the new railways will definitely require acquisition of private land?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Next, I touch on the issue of the Independent Safety Auditor.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Part 9 of the Bill provides for the appointment of an Independent Safety Auditor as well as rail safety inspectors.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: If the Government does not currently envisage these persons to perform these respective roles in terms of maintenance regimes for trains as well as infrastructure, will the Minister clarify who will perform such roles?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Should we, for example, not have a specific provision in the Bill for a maintenance auditor and inspectors, with necessary support from LTA?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: In light of the ongoing fiasco regarding the Singapore Mass Rapid Transit's (SMRT’s) maintenance efforts, I would urge the Government to put in place such measures at the beginning so that the cross-border railways can start with the right operational and maintenance regimes and the right corporate culture for operations and maintenance, and avoid the pitfalls we have seen with SMRT maintenance as well as LTA’s oversight of SMRT’s maintenance.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: As the cross-border railways involve two governments and possibly foreign concessionaires or licensees, this may be more complicated to manage.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Therefore, I hope the Government will get this right from the start so that we do not have this fiasco with poor operating conditions and maintenance down the road.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Next, I touch on the lack of provisions relating to conservation, environmental protection, public health risk, environmental impact assessment (EIA) and heritage impact assessment, as well as lack of provisions for public feedback and objections on these issues.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: This Bill involves a major construction project and long-term operation of regular high-speed rail services.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: However, the Bill is silent on conservation or environmental protection.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Construction and operation of the railway will affect the surrounding areas and have a detrimental impact on residents and businesses.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: There should be provisions for environmental, health and heritage impact assessments both before and during construction as well as periodically during operations to ensure that residents and businesses in the area are not adversely affected by the operations.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: If there are environmental or health risks, there should be provisions for mitigation with responsibilities between operators and regulators clearly spelt out.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: There should also be provisions regulating noise and other forms of pollution to protect people living or working nearby.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: There should be due diligence to ascertain: one, whether there are heritage sites nearby; two, if so, how they may be affected by the construction and operation of the railway; and three, what mitigation efforts should be put in place.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: We should have such measures in place at the onset before any problem even crops up.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Clause 5 of the Bill pertains to the preparation and publishing of railway plans and maps and the finality of such plans and maps.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Far beyond what are provided in clause 5, I think we should allow: one, greater public information about planning decisions before they are made; and two, public feedback about such planning decisions.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Will the Government consider incorporating similar provisions on the tendering of objections and representation as well as hearings and public inquiries seen in the Planning Act and Planning (Masterplan) Rules?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Next, I touch on the possibility of double punishment.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: I would also like to clarify with the Minister how the Government proposes to handle the possibility of both regulators from opposite sides of the Causeway meting out penalties against the concessionaire, licensees, operators or even subcontractors for the same infringements or breaches of any regulatory requirement.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Has the Malaysian Parliament introduced an equivalent Bill and looked into this issue?

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong (Non-Constituency Member)
text: Both regulators should make this clear to the concessionaire, licensees or operators at the onset.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: This Bill paves the way for its construction and it is heartening to see that we are moving swiftly along to the fruition of this ambitious project.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: I applaud the Government and all the hard work put in to ensure that this project is on track and on schedule.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Can the Minister shed light on this issue as it is on the minds of many Singaporeans?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: If the Minister is unable to provide further details at this point, can he at least clarify when such details will be available and whether his Ministry will be doing some form of public consultation with regard to this before any decision is being made?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Can the Minister clarify why there is a need for this new agency?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Can the Minister clarify if the security measures will be enhanced, compared with the existing Shuttle Tebrau operated by Keretapi Tanah Melayu (KTM) linking Johor Bahru and Singapore?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Would it be comparable to security measures at Changi Airport?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: The Minister also mentioned that LTA will be the cross-border railway security agency.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Will it not be better for the Singapore Police Force (SPF) to be this agency since the public transport security command (TRANSCOM) is currently under SPF?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Lastly, as its operations are cross-border, will we be working with relevant Malaysian agencies or persons to carry out its functions for this security agency?

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I am sure residents on both sides of the Causeway are very much looking forward to the greater access and convenience it will provide as well as the additional economic benefits to both nations.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: We can certainly expect a boost to tourism for both Singapore and Malaysia.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: In the future, travellers may even use it as a link to Thailand, Laos, China and other countries in south and central Asia and Europe.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: In fact, recently, I learned that Laos had started building a railway project linking China to Thailand.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: For example, what will be the estimated number of travellers per year; the planned economic activities and industrial developments around the railway; how many jobs will be created; and if there will be technology transfers and plans for the training of staff?

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: It is also important to quantify the expected impact on air travel and coach services once HSR starts its operations.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Would the Government share what is the agreed operating model and the finalised shareholding for HSR?

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Will the operation model of the railway station be similar to the existing service model at Changi Airport?

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I would also like to ask what will be the operator’s service recovery requirements to minimise service disruption.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: In the event of a potential terrorist attack, under what conditions would the Government be suspending the railway services?

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Would we need consensus from our Malaysian counterparts?

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Next, I seek details about the funding for the railway and the stations.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Will both governments issue bonds to investors to finance the entire project or raise funds through capital markets to allow Singaporeans and investors to own the equity of the operators or assets?

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Will there be rental and advertising revenue and which parties will be entitled to their collection?

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Residents have also asked me for the indicative ticket prices.

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: How will they be set and will they be benchmarked against comparable major cities with similar services?

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Will advance ticketing systems and cashless payment be introduced to allow customers to book via phone and online?

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Will the Government be connecting the railway station to the Jurong East MRT station and bus interchange for the convenience of passengers?

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: Will there be ample car park lots for business and day travellers who may leave their cars behind for the train ride?

speaker: Mr Gan Thiam Poh (Ang Mo Kio)
text: I conclude with my support for the Bill.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: The HSR and RTS Link are strategic projects that will significantly enhance connectivity between Singapore and Malaysia, strengthening the linkages between our economies and our peoples.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: I will try to answer each in turn.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: Mr Gan Thiam Poh asked about the economic benefits that the HSR will bring.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: Every day, more than 20,000 people travel between Singapore and KL.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: We expect a sizeable portion of these travellers to switch to HSR.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: The distance between KL and Singapore is about 350 kilometres, and this is widely regarded as a “sweet spot” or the ideal distance for HSR lines.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: Internationally, HSR lines of this distance have done very well.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: These include the London-Paris, Paris-Lyon and Tokyo-Osaka lines.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: We are confident that the HSR between Singapore and KL will be well-received.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: In addition, we expect HSR to catalyse new businesses and tourism between the two cities.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: Mr Dennis Tan and Mr Gan asked about the agreed operating model for HSR and how the Government intends to finance the project.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: Both countries have agreed on the commercial model for HSR.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: Singapore has appointed SG HSR Private Limited as our InfraCo.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: We are assessing what the most cost-efficient and appropriate way to finance SG HSR.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: Second, through an international tender, an Assets Company, or AssetsCo, will be appointed to provide and maintain the HSR trains and railway systems.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: Malaysia will separately appoint an OpCo Domestic to operate HSR services within Malaysia.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: The AssetsCo and OpCos will take care of their own financing.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: On the question of equity change from Mr Dennis Tan, the InfraCos of both Singapore and Malaysia will require the entities that are jointly appointed, like AssetsCo or OpCo International that I mentioned earlier, to seek specific approval before they can make significant changes to their equity composition.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: This will be stipulated in the contract rather than in the legislation.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: To facilitate the development of HSR and the RTS Link within Singapore, this Bill contains provisions similar to those found in existing Acts for public infrastructure.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: This includes the Rapid Transit Systems Act and the Street Works Act.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: The proposed clauses will ensure accountability and fair process in the planning and construction of cross-border railways.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: Mr Louis Ng and, in some aspects, Mr Dennis Tan, have asked about the potential impact of the HSR development on landowners and our green areas, and when details would be made available to the public.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: Detailed engineering studies to determine the railway alignment are ongoing.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: We expect to finalise these plans in the coming year or so.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: We will strive to minimise the impact of HSR development on landowners.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: However, should land acquisition or temporary displacement be needed, we will give sufficient time for occupants to relocate, specifically beyond two months.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: As part of the planning process, LTA will also study the environmental impact of the HSR project before finalising the design of HSR.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: Mr Gan Thiam Poh asked about the accessibility of the HSR terminus to local public transport options.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: The design work on the Jurong East terminus is still ongoing.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: However, the terminus will be close to two existing MRT lines at the Jurong East MRT Station, the North-South and East-West Lines, as well as new MRT lines, namely, the Jurong Regional Line and the Cross Island Line.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: It will also be next to the future integrated transport hub in Jurong East.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: All these will provide a wide range of local public transport options for any passengers coming to Singapore, which is also in line with our commitment to building a "car-lite" nation.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: Last but not least, I thank Mr Gan Thiam Poh for his suggestion to allocate ample taxi lanes to facilitate onward transfers.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: We will take this into consideration as part of our terminus design.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: Mr Gan Thiam Poh also asked if there will be advanced ticketing systems and cashless payments to allow customers to book tickets for HSR via phone or online.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: In October this year, LTA and MyHSR Corporation invited companies to share their experience in developing ticketing and fare collection systems.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: Our vision is for HSR to incorporate the latest ticketing technology and to deliver a seamless and passenger-friendly travel experience.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: As I mentioned earlier in my speech, the regulatory approach largely takes reference from our domestic railway experience but is adapted to suit the unique commercial and regulatory requirements of cross-border railway projects.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: Mr Gan Thiam Poh asked about how fares will be set and whether they will be benchmarked to similar services elsewhere.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: He also asked about the operator’s service recovery requirements.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: Commercial arrangements, such as performance standards and service recovery requirements, will be specified separately in contracts signed between the respective commercial entities.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: This is the common approach for railway projects that span across countries.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: Mr Dennis Tan asked about the maintenance regime and the auditors.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: And on double punishments that Mr Dennis Tan has asked, we will work with our Malaysian counterparts to harmonise the regulatory regime so that we would not have double punishments.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: On security regulation, Mr Louis Ng asked whether Singapore will be working with relevant Malaysian agencies and whether security measures will be enhanced compared to the existing KTM Berhad Tebrau Shuttle.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: Both countries have agreed on a common set of security outcomes to ensure that the cross-border railway operations are safe and secure.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: Detailed operating arrangements are being worked out by the agencies.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: For example, passengers travelling from Malaysia into Singapore via the HSR or RTS Link will be able to clear the immigration and security checks of both countries’ authorities before they board the train.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: Upon arrival into Singapore, passengers need not clear immigration and security checks a second time and can transfer seamlessly to local transport options.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: Mr Louis Ng asked about the rationale for appointing a cross-border railway security agency in Singapore under this Bill.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: A single cross-border railway security agency will help in coordinating regulatory and enforcement efforts across the various security agencies in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: As I have mentioned in my earlier speech, we intend to appoint LTA as the cross-border railway security agency, building on its current role in regulating and enforcing domestic public transport security.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: Mr Gan Thiam Poh asked about the situations in which the Government would consider suspending HSR operations and whether Malaysia’s concurrence would be needed.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: This is provided for in clause 56 of the Bill.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: The HSR and RTS Link projects are game changers that will draw the people of Singapore and Malaysia closer together, with a greater stake in each other’s continued growth and success.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: As we work with our Malaysian counterparts on the implementation of our cross-border railway projects, this Bill will provide LTA with the necessary powers to support the development of cross-border railways in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: It will also enable LTA to set out a robust regulatory framework for safe and secure cross-border railway operations.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: With this, Mr Speaker, I beg to move.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: Perhaps the Minister has overlooked this issue that I have raised.

speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: I raised the issue of a lack of provisions regarding conservation and environmental protection and public health with EIA and heritage impact assessment provisions, and public feedback as well.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: Minister, I just want to ask whether the results of the EIA will be made public and available online.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: Two, I hope that MOT will be engaging the green groups before publishing the results, so that we can consult them on their views again before the report is finalised.

speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng
text: We will take consultations with the different groups before making a final decision.
